title: Touch Design for Mobile Interfaces
edition: 2021 publication; no numbered edition stated on supplied title/copyright pages
extraction_notes: Title/copyright PDF1–3 and contents PDF6 inspected; foreword/introduction PDF7–18 read. PDF4–5 and19 are blank. Copyright2021 governs bibliographic identity, not2024 scan metadata.

Pypdf extraction of supplied ABBYY-processed PDF contains soft hyphens, broken line wraps, spaced headings, and flattened diagram/table layout. Critical visuals were separately rendered; no raw book text or images are distributed.

All chapter text PDF20–375 read across three bounded reader assignments; dividers and blank leaves were assessed, with no unread prose exclusions. Master checklist PDF376–383 also read. Index384–398 inventoried by boundary, not studied as new prose; printer mark/promotional/cover pages399–402 assessed and excluded from lessons.
PDF pages are one-based; chapter body printed labels are PDF minus1, verified in selected rendered pages. Divider and blank pages may not display a numeral.

Full-study describes text coverage, not exhaustive visual inspection. Thirty-five selected figure/table pages and one additional prose page were rendered. Other figures were understood from captions/surrounding prose only.

Underlying studies and historical standards cited by the author were not independently audited or replicated. Source assertions remain qualified; current platform guidance and operational recommendations are distinct.

chapters.title: Defining Mobile Devices
chapters.notes: TD-01. Full chapter text, including device-lab sidebar, read. Historical market/OS classifications are not adopted as current facts.

chapters.title: The History and Technology of Touch
chapters.notes: TD-02, TD-07. Full history, technology, keyscan/digitizer sidebars and gesture discussion read. No cited technical primary sources independently verified; hardware imperatives treated as contextual recommendations.

chapters.title: Capacitive Touch
chapters.notes: TD-02, TD-03. Full chapter read. Contact-patch/centroid/obscuration diagram on PDF67 visually inspected. Sensor and physiology assertions treated as author account, not universal current-device behavior.

chapters.title: Standards, Assumptions, and Problems
chapters.notes: TD-03, TD-04. Full chapter read. Finger/contact schematic on PDF80 inspected. Historical normative numbers not recast as current requirements; standards criticism does not authorize overriding binding guidance.

chapters.title: Finding Out How People Hold and Touch
chapters.notes: TD-01, TD-05, TD-06, TD-07, TD-08. Entire research narrative, figures captions, application guidance and checklist read. Eight figure pages inspected; historical samples, changing denominators, missing subgroup precision, and null-result limits recorded. No inference that all people can change grip or that demographics/access needs never matter.

chapters.title: Touch Accuracy and the Center-Out Preference
chapters.notes: TD-11/12. Complete extracted prose studied, including historical F-pattern discussion, author research method, positional accuracy, changing grips, center-oriented viewing, and kiosk exclusions. Divider114 and blank115 assessed. The numeric/center-out prescriptions are contextual source proposals, not current normative guidance.

chapters.title: How Fingers Get In the Way
chapters.notes: TD-13/14/15. Complete extracted prose studied, including contact patch versus occlusion, magnification, parallax, liftoff, pressed feedback, scrolling/content avoidance, two-axis and RTL qualifications. Divider142 and blank143 assessed. The left-alignment checklist is interpreted with explicit RTL context; no universal haptic, icon-label, or horizontal-scroll mandate adopted.

chapters.title: Imprecision and Probability
chapters.notes: TD-16/17. Complete extracted prose studied, including author-selected R95 tradeoff, near-miss overlays, actual hit areas, consequence-sensitive spacing, recovery, and resilience sidebar. Divider176 and blank177 assessed. Numeric probability and categorical anti-Cancel/Clear statements are not adopted as requirements.

chapters.title: Phones Are Not Flat
chapters.notes: TD-18/19/20. Complete extracted prose studied, including environmental/access conditions, encumbrance, repeated input, historical OS/browser edges, cases and bezels. Divider196 and blank197 assessed. Timeouts, bottom bars, 20% allowances, and accessibility completeness claims are contextualized rather than adopted literally.

chapters.title: People Only Touch What They See
chapters.notes: Read all extracted prose, captions, sidebars, checklists, and reference labels. Retained redundant cues, meaningful signifiers, viewing conditions, and feedback. Typography conversions, contrast claims, prevalence, shape psychology, and categorical styling/availability rules were assessed rather than adopted as specifications.

chapters.title: 1, 2, 3: Designing by Zones
chapters.notes: Read all chapter text and example discussion. Retained coherent task-based templates and direct-entry orientation. Fixed zone geometry, ranked visual attributes, heading counts, and simplified attention claims remain contextual author proposals.

chapters.title: Progressive Disclosure
chapters.notes: Read every disclosure/display method, benefit/downside list, historical example, and summary. Retained context, comparison, history, adaptive controls, data decision support, and discoverable collection extent. Strong tab/accordion/table/list prescriptions were explicitly bounded.

chapters.title: Practical Mobile Touchscreen Design
chapters.notes: Read all process sections, technology assertions, recommended-reference prose, and final summary. Retained audience/context investigation, actual capability checks, iterative delivery, and method-matched evaluation. Linked works and claims were not independently verified; no participant or physical calibration activity occurred.

figure_checks.description: Contact patch, centroid, and obscured area shown separately on a held-phone illustration.
figure_checks.inspection: Visually checked the three distinct labels and arrows: the covered area extends beyond the contact patch. Conceptual image does not supply target dimensions or demonstrate every device reports the centroid.

figure_checks.description: Finger profile and small contact patch below the screen line.
figure_checks.inspection: Visually inspected finger-size and contact-patch labels and categorical caption. Diagram distinguishes quantities but cannot establish a universal zero correlation between size and accuracy.

figure_checks.description: 2013 holding/interaction summary pie with grip sketches, listening icon and calling icon.
figure_checks.inspection: Verified listening and talking categories coexist with touch grips. No numeric percentage labels or subgroup denominators in figure; do not substitute the780 touching subset as denominator for the whole pie.

figure_checks.description: Six illustrated phone grip/interaction forms.
figure_checks.inspection: Read all six labels and examined hand arrangements: cradled, held-and-tapped, two hands landscape, one hand first/second order, and two hands portrait. Taxonomy illustration is not a preference ranking or exhaustive access model.

figure_checks.description: Hold/tap bar chart for historically over-five-inch phones.
figure_checks.inspection: Compared relative heights: held-and-tapped highest, cradled next, one-hand/thumb and two-finger/thumb lower. Vertical axis has no numeric calibration; exact percentages and population certainty cannot be recovered.

figure_checks.description: Body position/activity trend by illustrated device size with approximate viewing-distance endpoints.
figure_checks.inspection: Read standing/walking versus sitting/reclining regions and approximate25cm/60cm endpoint labels. Device silhouettes have no measured class definitions, confidence intervals, or subgroup counts; treated as trend illustration.

figure_checks.description: Stacked device-support trend: in hand, on a surface, in a stand.
figure_checks.inspection: Verified larger illustrative devices show greater surface/stand share. Y-axis endpoints0/100% but no per-class counts or precision; no exact layout breakpoint inferred.

figure_checks.description: Four still frames from a usability test described as four interaction changes in14seconds.
figure_checks.inspection: Inspected visibly different hand positions in the four frames. Images establish illustrated variation; still frames do not independently establish timing, transition sequence, frequency, or causality.

figure_checks.description: Stacked grip-type bars for tapping a link, checkbox, typing, short scrolling, and long scrolling.
figure_checks.inspection: Matched color legend to grip sketches; typing has a visibly larger two-finger/thumb component. Bars show different task mixes but do not provide subgroup sample sizes or uncertainty.

figure_checks.description: Phone and tablet/laptop viewing drawings with projected sight lines.
figure_checks.inspection: Examined relative distance and visual-angle depiction. This is an explanatory diagram, not a validated universal size/distance formula or measurement of a user population.
